rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act – prohibition on algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Rental property owners may not pay for or use the services of a coordinator (algorithmic revenue management software or device performing a coordinating function), and no person may perform a coordinating function, facilitate anticompetitive agreements among rental property owners, or engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination. Violations are violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act.

exemption_conditions.condition: Residential dwelling unit does not include inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, or detention or correctional facilities
Coordinator does not include a government entity setting or limiting rents through affordability controls in accordance with law

coverage.notes: Applies to rental property owners (owning one or more rental residential dwelling units), coordinators, and any person performing a coordinating function. Algorithmic device excludes non-AI spreadsheets requiring human analysis and databases that only query unprocessed data.

rules.coverage_text: Applies to rental property owners of residential dwelling units (houses, apartments, accessory units or other units intended as a primary residence in NJ), their agents, coordinators, and any person performing a coordinating function or parallel pricing coordination.
rules.exemptions: Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention/correctional facilities. Coordinating function excludes use of competitively sensitive information solely for research/statistical analysis/testing not used to set prices; free public rent estimates; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set/recommend prices or collect sensitive info for that purpose; and government entities setting rents through affordability controls. Algorithmic device excludes non-AI spreadsheets requiring human analysis and databases that only query unprocessed data.
rules.interaction: Violations are violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act (C.56:9-1 et seq.), with sections 6-17 of that act applicable; the act is in addition to existing antitrust law. Municipalities are prohibited from enacting ordinances that conflict with the act (except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law).
